headline: Practical guidance recommends especially strict delays after photodynamic therapy drugs, while many other photosensitizing medications warrant caution, test spots, and wavelength review rather than automatic exclusion.
implication: Useful as a pragmatic comparator for medication-screening language.
caveat: Consensus guidance for non-essential aesthetic lasers and IPLs, not peer-reviewed whole-body PBM evidence.

headline: Registry identifies the sham-controlled fibromyalgia whole-body PBM program but does not contribute extracted outcome results here.
implication: Useful for trial identification, comparator boundaries, and registry linkage.
caveat: Accessible registry extraction was sparse and did not expose posted results or detailed enrollment fields.

headline: Registry identifies a completed whole-body PBM fibromyalgia trial focused on circadian blood pressure, but no extracted results are included here.
implication: Useful for trial tracking and endpoint framing around autonomic physiology.
caveat: The accessible registry extract did not expose detailed enrollment or results tables.

headline: Registry describes a direct NovoTHOR whole-body PBM implementation for sleep and performance, but no outcome results are available in the record used here.
implication: Useful for protocol cadence, endpoint selection, and exclusion boundaries.
caveat: Single-arm open-label registry with no placebo group and no extracted efficacy results.

headline: Registry describes a direct NovoTHOR whole-body PBM implementation for sleep and performance, but no outcome results are available in the record used here.
implication: Useful for protocol cadence, endpoint selection, and exclusion boundaries.
caveat: Single-arm open-label registry with no placebo group and no extracted efficacy results.

headline: Registry describes a direct NovoTHOR whole-body PBM implementation for sleep and performance, but no outcome results are available in the record used here.
implication: Useful for protocol cadence, endpoint selection, and exclusion boundaries.
caveat: Single-arm open-label registry with no placebo group and no extracted efficacy results.

headline: Registry includes a direct whole-body PBM arm in older adults, but no outcome results are available in the record used here.
implication: Useful for older-adult protocol variants, endpoint selection, and adherence expectations.
caveat: Three-arm open-label non-placebo registry; the record alone cannot establish a whole-body effect.

headline: Registry includes a direct whole-body PBM arm in older adults, but no outcome results are available in the record used here.
implication: Useful for older-adult protocol variants, endpoint selection, and adherence expectations.
caveat: Three-arm open-label non-placebo registry; the record alone cannot establish a whole-body effect.

headline: Completed registry materials suggest timing-dependent benefits for CK and soreness, but neither pre- nor post-exercise whole-body PBM improved muscle performance.
implication: Useful for sham-controlled sports implementation details and for separating soreness or biomarker signals from performance claims.
caveat: Evidence comes from registry materials and an attached report rather than a linked peer-reviewed publication in this batch.

headline: Hypertension registry compares one full-body 660 nm LED panel session against modified ILIB and matched sham on acute vascular endpoints.
implication: Useful for acute cardiometabolic endpoint design and exclusion-based safety boundaries, while keeping it separate from direct red-plus-near-infrared protocol claims.
caveat: Registry only, disease-specific, and mixed with a modified ILIB arm; no efficacy results are available.

headline: This registry studies how much 660 nm and 850 nm light is reflected during non-contact whole-body PBM across skin phototype and sex, but it does not report clinical efficacy outcomes.
implication: Useful for device geometry, non-contact dosing assumptions, and phototype-related light-loss considerations.
caveat: Healthy-volunteer dosimetry registry rather than a therapeutic efficacy study.

headline: Triple-blind placebo-controlled diabetes registry plans 20-minute whole-body PBM sessions with fasting glucose, HbA1c, and sleep-quality follow-up.
implication: Useful for tracking disease-specific implementation choices and longer follow-up endpoints without treating the registry as outcome evidence.
caveat: Registry protocol only; no efficacy results are reported, and the population is restricted to adults with stable type 2 diabetes.

headline: Recruiting registry describes a season-long whole-body PBM soccer protocol with repeated soreness, strength, jump, blood-count, and PSQI endpoints, but no outcomes are available yet.
implication: Useful for protocol cadence, endpoint selection, and planned safety boundaries in a sports setting.
caveat: Registry protocol only; no efficacy or adverse-event outcomes have been reported in the extracted materials.

headline: Parkinson's registry plans about 30 whole-body PBM sessions over 10 weeks with motor, balance, cognitive, and safety endpoints.
implication: Useful for neurologic-disease implementation recall and safety screening, but not for efficacy claims because the study is open-label and single-arm.
caveat: Registry-only, uncontrolled, and disease-specific; no placebo arm or results are available.

headline: Acute whole-body PBM did not outperform placebo on the Illinois Agility Test in a preliminary trained-participant crossover study.
implication: Useful for recall of an abstract-only implementation variant and for preserving another null performance result.
caveat: Conference supplement abstract with only 10 participants and limited methodological detail.

headline: This supervised single-arm whole-body NovoTHOR feasibility study reported broad symptom improvement and high acceptability after 18 sessions, but it has no control group and remains a preprint with title-metadata conflict.
implication: Useful for disease-specific supervised implementation context and candidate outcome selection, not as a direct consumer efficacy claim.
caveat: Accessible source surfaces disagree on whether the title is chronic-pain or fibromyalgia focused; the study is uncontrolled, preprint-only, and includes internal dose-reporting inconsistencies that should not be normalized away.

headline: Review says PBM-sleep research is promising but still early, heterogeneous, and under-standardized.
implication: Useful for mechanism mapping, safety boundaries, and endpoint ideas, not for direct whole-body efficacy claims.
caveat: Most summarized studies are transcranial, cervical, case-report, or special-population studies; only limited whole-body evidence appears.

headline: Fibromyalgia systematic review reported overall PBMT benefit and suggested more sustained effects for whole-body delivery than localized treatment.
implication: Useful for comparing sibling variants and locating relevant fibromyalgia trials, but not for direct protocol claims.
caveat: The review combines localized and whole-body delivery modes, heterogeneous protocols, and studies with varied risk of bias.

headline: Scoping review mapped promising but heterogeneous fibromyalgia PBMT evidence and argued that many NICE concerns may be addressable by existing literature.
implication: Useful for evidence mapping, policy framing, and identification of experiential outcomes.
caveat: Scoping review methodology does not provide pooled effect estimates or a direct causal summary; cost-effectiveness remains unresolved.

headline: Suspended registry describes an acute rugby crossover protocol testing whole-body PBM before isokinetic fatigue and DOMS assessment, but no results are posted.
implication: Useful for source recall, preconditioning timing variants, and endpoint planning.
caveat: Suspended status and absence of results make this protocol-only context.

headline: Recruiting registry tests acute full-body PBM against placebo in trained men with torque, fatigue, agility, soreness, and perceived recovery outcomes.
implication: Useful for source recall and for tracking a larger planned follow-up to earlier preliminary sports studies.
caveat: Registry only; no outcome data yet.

headline: Dose-response diabetes registry specifies 10-, 20-, and 30-minute 850 nm whole-body PBM tiers with capillary glucose monitoring through 24 hours.
implication: Useful for dose-range recall and glucose endpoint timing, while keeping single-wavelength near-infrared-only exposure separate from direct red-plus-near-infrared claims.
caveat: Registry-only with no results, male-only disease cohort, and an internal sample-size inconsistency between the target field and arm description.

headline: COPD crossover registry uses Joovv Elite whole-body light and sham to study dyspnea, fatigue, functional tests, and respiratory pressures.
implication: Useful for extending recall beyond pain and sport into respiratory disease and function-oriented endpoints in a supervised whole-body PBM setting.
caveat: Registry protocol only; no efficacy results are posted, and exertional safety boundaries are explicit.

headline: FDA defines PBM as non-heating light therapy and expects wavelength, dose, irradiance, pulsing, target-area, and safety reporting in premarket submissions.
implication: Useful for device-description completeness and for keeping whole-body claims inside nonthermal, safety-aware boundaries.
caveat: Draft nonbinding regulatory guidance rather than a clinical efficacy study.

headline: IARC classifies UV-emitting tanning devices as carcinogenic to humans.
implication: This is the sharpest authoritative boundary against using sunbed or tanning-device comparisons in a whole-body red/NIR protocol.
caveat: The source addresses ultraviolet carcinogenicity, not therapeutic photobiomodulation.

headline: NICE concluded that evidence for intranasal phototherapy in allergic rhinitis was limited in quantity and quality and should remain in research settings.
implication: This is a strong external-protocol boundary source showing that nearby intranasal light procedures should not be generalized into whole-body PBM claims.
caveat: NICE specifically requested better reporting of wavelength, intensity, duration, repeated use, and long-term safety.

headline: NIHR listing confirms a UK whole-body PBM chronic-pain study, but it does not contribute extracted outcome results.
implication: Useful for recruitment timing, public-trial discoverability, and protocol linkage.
caveat: Registry-style listing only; no extracted enrollment, effect estimates, or adverse-event results.

headline: An early 590 nm full-panel facial photomodulation cohort reported photoaging improvement in 90% of participants with no side effects noted.
implication: Useful only as adjacent panel-based cosmetic context; it does not directly test whole-body red and near-infrared exposure.
caveat: This was an uncontrolled face-focused amber/yellow LED study with abstract-level detail only.

headline: Eight 590 nm full-face LED treatments were associated with clinical, profilometric, and histologic photoaging improvements.
implication: Useful as adjacent panel-based skin-rejuvenation context and for candidate tissue endpoints, but not as direct whole-body red/NIR evidence.
caveat: This was a face-only 590 nm cosmetic study with no sham control and a major population mismatch versus Murph.

headline: Combined 633/830 nm LED therapy improved periorbital profilometry and subjective photoaging measures in an older clinic-style study.
implication: Supports biological/clinical plausibility for red+NIR facial photorejuvenation.
caveat: Professional workflow and older cohort-style design limit direct transfer to modern home masks.

headline: Combined 633 nm and 830 nm facial LED therapy improved wrinkle-related profilometry and patient-reported softness in a small single-arm study.
implication: Useful as adjacent facial parameter and tolerability context, but not direct whole-body evidence.
caveat: Single-arm local facial study with small numbers and non-systemic endpoints.

headline: Combined 633/830 nm LED treatment reported wrinkle/profilometry improvement and collagen ultrastructure changes.
implication: Adds supportive red+NIR photoaging evidence and mechanistic plausibility.
caveat: Control status was not extracted and the study appears closer to a clinical cohort than a rigorous home-mask trial.

headline: Nine combined 633/830 nm facial LED treatments were associated with wrinkle improvement and thicker collagen fibers on electron microscopy.
implication: Useful as adjacent facial red-plus-NIR skin context and biopsy vocabulary, but not as direct whole-body evidence.
caveat: No control arm, local cosmetic population, and biopsy data were limited to a small subset.

headline: Far-infrared sauna evidence suggests some cardiovascular or pain signals but also clear null findings, and it belongs to a thermal-sauna intervention class rather than nonthermal PBM.
implication: Useful for keeping infrared-sauna claims from being conflated with whole-body red/NIR photobiomodulation claims.
caveat: The review identified only nine relevant papers and many domains were supported by single studies.

headline: Nightly whole-body red-light exposure improved sleep quality, increased serum melatonin, and improved 12-minute run performance in elite female basketball players.
implication: Important adjacent evidence for sleep-related and endurance-related signals from repeated whole-body light exposure.
caveat: This was red light only, not a red-plus-near-infrared protocol, and it was tested in a small elite athlete cohort.

headline: Large-area red and red/NIR light-panel exposure improved skin texture and collagen-related measures, but broadband red/NIR did not clearly outperform red-only exposure.
implication: Useful for dose, endpoint, and device-geometry context when considering skin photobiomodulation outcomes.
caveat: Large-area light panels are not the same intervention geometry as a consumer facial red+NIR mask; the red-only versus broadband comparison limits NIR-specific claims.

headline: Large-area and full-body polychromatic PBM improved cosmetic skin outcomes versus control, but broader 570–850 nm output did not outperform red-only treatment.
implication: Useful as sibling evidence for large-area delivery feasibility and skin endpoint selection, not as direct evidence for whole-body wellness outcomes.
caveat: This was a cosmetic/photoaging trial with varied irradiances and treatment durations across groups, and it did not test a Murph-style whole-body wellness protocol.

headline: The small literature identified no reported complications from laser treatment in patients taking photosensitizing medication, but only four publications were found.
implication: Supports a caution-not-blanket-contraindication approach when wavelength and medication activation spectra are considered.
caveat: Sparse evidence, non-PBM laser contexts, and little direct relevance to whole-body red/NIR beds.

headline: This editorial supports using photobiomodulation therapy terminology rather than older low-level light or laser labels.
implication: Useful for naming the family and modality consistently without implying a different intervention.
caveat: No abstract or outcome data were exposed; terminology source only.

headline: The dedicated eye-safety review found ocular complaints but little evidence of ocular damage in healthy unmedicated light-therapy users, with uncertainty for ocular disease or photosensitivity.
implication: Outdoor-light protocols should flag ocular disease, photosensitizing drugs, and visual discomfort as reasons for clinician/eye-care review and conservative dosing.
caveat: The evidence is mainly UV-filtered therapeutic light rather than direct sunlight.

headline: Light therapy appeared ophthalmologically safe in physically healthy, unmedicated people, but one photosensitized maculopathy case and poor reporting justify conservative eye-safety language.
implication: Supports eye protection and extra caution in people with ocular disease or photosensitizing medications.
caveat: Most included studies were not whole-body red/NIR PBM, and reporting of light parameters was poor.

headline: RCT evidence for LED dermatology exists, but strength varies by condition and study quality.
implication: Use this as context for the LED dermatology evidence base and for identifying older controlled trials.
caveat: The review covers many dermatologic indications; its evidence grades should not be promoted into direct red/NIR photoaging claims.

headline: A dermatology LED review found generally few reported adverse events, but the evidence base was heterogeneous and often methodologically weak.
implication: Useful for safety framing and for documenting why Murph should not overclaim from small, mixed dermatology studies.
caveat: This review spans many skin conditions and wavelengths and is not specific to whole-body red and near-infrared exposure.

headline: Cancer-PBM literature remained mixed at the preclinical level, which is why oncology exposure should stay in a supervised safety-boundary bucket.
implication: Use for uncertainty framing around malignancy, not to infer benefit or harm from whole-body consumer use.
caveat: Narrative review with no new participant data and mixed cell-line findings.

headline: Laser and LED PBM share wavelength ranges but differ in delivery, geometry, and practical use.
implication: Use to avoid assuming that laser and LED evidence is interchangeable for skin photoaging.
caveat: Broad PBM device review; not a direct clinical trial of red/NIR skin texture.

headline: The review argues LEDs are a durable PBM delivery class with practical advantages for large-area treatment, but laser and LED outputs should not be treated as automatically equivalent.
implication: Useful for explaining why whole-body beds are LED-heavy and why laser-derived PBM evidence should be translated carefully.
caveat: Perspective review rather than a direct laser-versus-LED whole-body comparative trial.

headline: The review describes preliminary antidepressant and mechanistic signals for transcranial or systemic PBM, but evidence quality was limited and not specific to whole-body exposure.
implication: Useful for mood-claim boundaries and mechanism notes, while preserving the distinction between psychiatric PBM studies and whole-body wellness use.
caveat: Most clinical studies lacked an appropriate control and treatment parameters varied substantially.

headline: This review frames PBM efficacy as highly parameter-sensitive, with contradictory findings often linked to wavelength, fluence, irradiance, pulsing, and repetition differences.
implication: Useful for normalizing whole-body device claims and for avoiding overconfident dose translation across devices or tissues.
caveat: Narrative review spanning mixed laboratory, animal, and clinical models rather than a direct whole-body intervention trial.

headline: Recommendations paper argues that PBMT has a dose window and that future sports trials need stronger reporting, but it is built mainly on localized PBMT evidence rather than whole-body trials.
implication: Useful for methodological and dosimetry framing, not for direct whole-body efficacy claims.
caveat: The cited evidence base is mostly localized muscle PBM and includes low-to-moderate certainty evidence.

headline: Across 27 included supportive-care oncology PBMT reports, most studies reported no side effects and the review did not identify a tumor-safety signal.
implication: Useful for safety framing when malignancy or recurrence concerns are raised, but it does not establish efficacy or direct whole-body safety.
caveat: Included studies were heterogeneous and long-term recurrence data remained limited.

headline: Localized PBM was recommended for prevention of oral mucositis in specific supervised oncology settings, with no general treatment recommendation and no parameter interchangeability.
implication: This is foundational for separating supervised localized oncology PBM protocols from whole-body red/NIR home or wellness protocols.
caveat: The guideline explicitly warns clinicians to follow all parameters of selected protocols and not interchange them.

headline: High-fluence red LED safety differed by skin phenotype, with dose-limiting reactions at very high fluences.
implication: Use as a safety-boundary source for dose ceilings, skin-of-color caution, and monitoring for erythema, hyperpigmentation, or blistering—not as anti-aging efficacy evidence.
caveat: Forearm safety results do not prove facial texture or wrinkle improvement.

headline: Human red-LED skin exposure was tolerated without serious adverse events, but dose-limiting blistering and prolonged erythema appeared at higher fluences and tolerability differed by race or ethnicity.
implication: Best human skin-safety anchor in this batch for setting conservative fluence ceilings and watch-fors.
caveat: Local forearm exposure in supervised trials is not the same as whole-body wellness use.

headline: Meta-analysis found better cognitive performance after transcranial PBM in young healthy adults, but the intervention was focal brain-directed PBM rather than whole-body exposure.
implication: Useful to document that cognition claims in the PBM literature mostly come from transcranial studies, not whole-body light beds.
caveat: The review reported heterogeneity, modest overall quality, and publication-bias signals, so even transcranial claims should be framed cautiously.

headline: Bright-light therapy showed modest antidepressant benefit in seasonal affective disorder, but this is bright-light psychiatry evidence rather than whole-body PBM evidence.
implication: This is a high-value mood-disorder boundary source for preventing bright-light SAD literature from being generalized into whole-body red/NIR claims.
caveat: Most included trials were small, short term, and at elevated risk of bias, and placebo credibility remained a recurrent concern.

headline: Intranasal PBM is positioned as a distinct local or systemic-adjacent PBM strategy, not as whole-body exposure.
implication: Useful for separating intranasal device claims from whole-body PBM claims while preserving proposed blood-flow and blood-rheology mechanisms.
caveat: The review notes that no clinical studies of implanted deep-nasal PBMT had been conducted and that comparative sham studies were still needed.

headline: This commentary emphasizes that existing in vivo and clinical PBMT evidence is more relevant than theoretical in vitro concern when judging tumor safety.
implication: Useful as interpretive context for oncology safety debates, not as standalone evidence.
caveat: No new participant data were reported and no abstract was available in the accessible PubMed record.

headline: In vitro oncology PBMT signals were conflicting, but in vivo and clinical studies with follow-up generally supported safety regarding tumor growth at recommended parameters.
implication: Useful for separating theoretical cell-culture concerns from supervised clinical evidence.
caveat: The evidence mix spanned cell, animal, and clinical studies, so it is not a direct consumer whole-body safety study.

headline: Five-minute full-body PBM after matches did not improve most hormonal, inflammatory, autonomic, strength, or jump recovery measures in young water polo athletes.
implication: Useful as a direct null or mixed athlete-recovery study for post-match full-body LED panel dosing.
caveat: Small preliminary tournament study with only 13 young male athletes and one isolated LDH finding.

headline: Pre- and post-exercise whole-body light-bed PBM did not significantly lower creatine kinase or salivary interleukin-6 after intense resistance exercise.
implication: Useful for dosing, device geometry, and null-biomarker boundaries in athlete settings.
caveat: Small male-only crossover trial without a convincing sham and with non-contact light-bed exposure geometry.

headline: In a 30-participant single-arm neck-device study, 16 weeks of 630/850 nm exposure showed no significant thyroid or parathyroid changes while local wrinkle and skin measures improved.
implication: Useful for adjacent thyroid-safety boundary setting around neck exposure and for local device parameter context.
caveat: This was a neck-only single-arm cosmetic study in healthy women, so it does not directly establish whole-body safety or efficacy.

headline: In 693 HCT patients followed up to 15 years, PBMT for oral mucositis was not associated with immediate adverse effects or oral secondary malignancy.
implication: Strongest long-term oncology safety anchor in the batch, but still a retrospective supervised-care context.
caveat: Single-center retrospective oncology cohort with oral-mucositis protocols, not direct whole-body wellness use.

headline: Drug-induced photosensitivity can arise from phototoxic or photoallergic mechanisms under sunlight or artificial light.
implication: Protocol guidance should advise medication-label review and clinician/pharmacist input for known photosensitizers.
caveat: Mechanistic and safety source, not a protocol-outcome study.

headline: Drug-induced photosensitivity can involve UV and visible light, so medication screening matters even when a protocol is not UV-based.
implication: Supports medication review and caution language for people with known photosensitivity risks.
caveat: General dermatology review, not a PBM trial and not specific to whole-body red/NIR devices.

headline: Narrative review summarizes potential sports benefits and mechanisms for PBM, while emphasizing that dosage and treatment parameters are not yet standardized.
implication: Useful for mechanism and source-network context, but too broad and too localized-literature-heavy to support a direct whole-body claim.
caveat: Narrative review without pooled effect estimates and with major dependence on non-whole-body sports PBM studies.

headline: Protocol defines a 12-session whole-body NovoTHOR versus placebo fibromyalgia RCT with extensive follow-up and mechanistic endpoints.
implication: Best source in this batch for exact planned device parameters, sham-controlled design, and endpoint schedule.
caveat: Protocol paper only; no efficacy or adverse-event results were available from this source alone.

headline: Protocol defines a 12-session whole-body NovoTHOR versus placebo fibromyalgia RCT with extensive follow-up and mechanistic endpoints.
implication: Best source in this batch for exact planned device parameters, sham-controlled design, and endpoint schedule.
caveat: Protocol paper only; no efficacy or adverse-event results were available from this source alone.

headline: Protocol outlines a supervised NHS whole-body NovoTHOR feasibility pathway for chronic pain, but no efficacy results are reported.
implication: Useful for supervised scheduling, eligibility, and outcome selection in chronic pain rather than for generalized protocol claims.
caveat: Single-arm protocol with target enrollment of 20; no completed outcome or adverse-event results were available in this record.

headline: Season-long full-body PBM use was associated with lower sleeping heart rate, but also with shorter total and REM sleep on post-treatment nights.
implication: Useful for operational cadence and wearable endpoint selection, while preserving a possible trade-off between cardiorespiratory recovery signals and sleep duration.
caveat: Observational team data with no placebo and with sleep-stage estimates from a wearable ring rather than polysomnography.

headline: Commentary argues PBM may improve sleep, especially via nocturnal transcranial mechanisms, but it does not provide direct whole-body efficacy data.
implication: Useful for pathway hypotheses and source recall, not to support a whole-body benefit claim.
caveat: This is a narrative commentary focused mainly on transcranial and nighttime brain mechanisms.

headline: The WALT position paper reports robust supportive-care PBM evidence with no demonstrated clinical adverse events, but still calls for caution in cancer populations and long follow-up.
implication: Useful for expert-practice boundaries and parameter-reporting expectations, not as direct whole-body consumer evidence.
caveat: Consensus guidance rather than a new comparative trial.

headline: A recent meta-analysis assessed LED skin therapy across heterogeneous indications.
implication: Use for broad LED evidence mapping and source snowballing, not as standalone proof for this red/NIR photoaging protocol.
caveat: Full effect estimates and subgroup details were not extracted from accessible full text in this batch; do not infer direct photoaging efficacy.

headline: This dermatology LED meta-analysis showed strong pooled acne effects and positive direction for some yellow/NIR applications, but important heterogeneity for other conditions.
implication: Helpful for cataloging dermatology effect-size context and heterogeneity, not for direct whole-body efficacy claims.
caveat: The included studies covered multiple wavelengths, indications, and local skin applications rather than whole-body exposure.

headline: Placebo-controlled fibromyalgia RCT reported physiologic changes in circadian blood pressure, tenderness thresholds, and tissue elasticity after whole-body PBM.
implication: Useful for mechanistic and measurement-oriented endpoints rather than for broad symptom generalization.
caveat: Small sample, variable treatment timing, and biomarker-focused outcomes limit extrapolation; adverse-event detail was not prominent in the accessible extraction.

headline: Short-term placebo-controlled fibromyalgia RCT found significant benefit on pain, quality of life, kinesiophobia, and self-efficacy after whole-body PBM.
implication: This is direct supervised efficacy evidence for a fibromyalgia sibling variant and a key source for short-term endpoint direction.
caveat: Pain catastrophizing did not differ between groups, follow-up was short, and the disease-specific supervised cohort limits direct reuse for generalized protocol claims.

headline: Highest-dose daytime 850 nm PBM improved mood, drowsiness, IFN-gamma, and resting heart rate in winter, but did not improve sleep or circadian outcomes.
implication: Useful as adjacent human dosing and outcome evidence for systemic PBM effects, but not as a direct whole-body sleep-efficacy claim.
caveat: Illumination was limited to face, neck, and hands; season subgroup sizes were small.

headline: Human transcranial PBM studies report altered brain activity and regional blood flow, but the exposure geometry is focal and head-only.
implication: Useful for mechanism and endpoint context while keeping transcranial brain-stimulation claims separate from whole-body red/NIR exposure claims.
caveat: Patient data were sparse and methods were heterogeneous, so this review should not be promoted into direct whole-body efficacy language.

headline: Bright-light therapy in insomnia showed pooled benefit mainly for wake after sleep onset, with no clear pooled benefit for several other sleep metrics.
implication: This is a core boundary source for preventing bright-light insomnia literature from being treated as whole-body red/NIR PBM evidence.
caveat: The accessible primary excerpts supported pooled effect sizes for WASO but did not expose a stable total participant count for the whole synthesis.

headline: Open-label long-COVID pilot reported cognitive and qEEG improvements after both transcranial and whole-body PBM, but the mixed-modality, no-placebo design keeps it out of direct protocol claims.
implication: Useful for symptom-cluster recall and tolerability in a different symptomatic population, while preserving strong design and directness limits.
caveat: Only 14 completers, 7 in the whole-body arm, with repeated cognitive testing, no placebo arm, and a paper that mixes transcranial and whole-body modalities.

headline: Twenty minutes of whole-body PBM before repeated Wingate cycling did not improve performance, lactate, perceived recovery, or most physiological responses, but next-morning rMSSD was higher than after placebo.
implication: Useful as adjacent athlete evidence showing an acute recovery signal without a same-day performance effect.
caveat: Most details available here come from the abstract; dosing specifics beyond session duration were not fully exposed in the accessible primary record.

headline: Single-arm fibromyalgia feasibility trial reported acceptable delivery and broad symptom improvement after 18 whole-body PBMT sessions.
implication: Useful for acceptability, adherence, and candidate endpoint selection in supervised fibromyalgia delivery.
caveat: No control group; 19 of 21 participants completed the course; symptom changes cannot be attributed causally to PBMT from this study alone.

headline: Two red-light myopia devices approached or exceeded retinal photochemical safety limits during intended continuous viewing.
implication: Supports strict eye-protection and no-direct-gaze language for bright red-light devices.
caveat: This was a device-output analysis for ophthalmic instruments, not a whole-body PBM clinical study.

headline: Longer-term placebo-controlled fibromyalgia RCT reported benefits across pain, quality of life, activity, kinesiophobia, and self-efficacy after whole-body PBM.
implication: This is the strongest direct long-term symptom paper in the batch for the fibromyalgia sibling variant.
caveat: Pain was not clearly different at the 3-month timepoint, catastrophizing improved only at 6 months, and placebo improvements complicate attribution.

headline: Qualitative interviews described a positive recovery-like process during whole-body PBMT, but this is experiential rather than controlled efficacy evidence.
implication: Useful for implementation, acceptability, and subjective change domains.
caveat: Small convenience sample from a treatment cohort with no placebo comparison for the interview data.

headline: A sham-controlled home-use LED neck device trial reported improved neck-wrinkle scores, with mixed investigator-versus-participant global-aesthetic ratings.
implication: Supports the feasibility of home-use LED exposure schedules and neck-specific outcome measurement.
caveat: Neck anatomy and device geometry differ from the target facial-mask protocol; participant GAIS was not consistently significant in extracted summaries.

headline: A sham-controlled neck-device trial found better investigator-rated wrinkle outcomes and no thyroid-related complications, but participant-rated GAIS did not clearly separate groups.
implication: Useful for neck-adjacent safety framing and sham-controlled device parameters, but still a local cosmetic neck study.
caveat: Manufacturer funding and the cosmetic neck population limit generalization to whole-body Murph use.

headline: Ocular Complication in Facial Aesthetic Laser and Light Treatments: A Comprehensive Review
implication: Use as safety-boundary context; do not promote to direct skin efficacy evidence.
caveat: Mostly professional laser/light procedures rather than low-power home red/NIR skin protocols.

headline: Facial light and laser procedures can cause conjunctival, corneal, and retinal injuries when protection is inadequate or positioning is poor.
implication: Supports protective eyewear, positioning, and movement-control instructions for any face-adjacent exposure.
caveat: Aesthetic facial procedures are adjacent, not direct whole-body wellness protocols.

headline: Across pediatric red-light myopia studies, no irreversible visual harm was identified, but reversible retinal findings and afterimages justify monitoring.
implication: Useful for ocular monitoring language, not as direct support for whole-body PBM.
caveat: The population was children receiving ophthalmic red-light exposure, not adults using whole-body devices.

headline: Across five athlete studies, whole-body PBM showed limited sleep-related signals but no convincing benefit for exercise performance or recovery biomarkers.
implication: Useful as the best current corpus map for exercise-timed whole-body PBM, while preserving that these are adjacent athlete-focused variants rather than direct general-protocol efficacy evidence.
caveat: Only five heterogeneous studies were included, and all were athlete or physically active populations.

headline: Home red plus near-infrared periocular mask improved crow's-feet grades versus sham in a blinded randomized study.
implication: Supports including periocular wrinkle texture as a protocol-relevant outcome for home red/NIR masks.
caveat: The endpoint is crow's feet rather than full-face texture, and the population was Asian-descent adults with selected skin types and baseline grades.

headline: A sham-controlled 630/850 nm periocular mask trial found significant wrinkle-score improvements and described treatment as safe, well tolerated, and painless.
implication: Useful only as adjacent local face-mask context and tolerability context, not as direct whole-body evidence.
caveat: The outcomes were periocular cosmetic measures in an Asian facial-aging population.

headline: A 660 nm red LED mask frequency trial found no significant blinded WAS difference but did find ImageJ wrinkle-length and satisfaction improvements versus sham.
implication: Useful for frequency and endpoint-selection boundaries, especially that different wrinkle measures can disagree.
caveat: The intervention was red-only rather than red plus near-infrared, and the population was women aged 45-60 years.

headline: A facial rejuvenation frequency trial found null photographic wrinkle-score differences but positive ImageJ and satisfaction signals, with no clear gain from the higher session frequency.
implication: Useful as adjacent evidence about dose frequency and mixed endpoint behavior in local facial PBM.
caveat: This was a face-only 660 nm cosmetic protocol in women, not a whole-body red/NIR exposure study.

headline: Consensus panel found PBM generally safe in adults and separated supported clinical indications from less certain uses.
implication: Use for adult safety framing and to avoid overstating cosmetic photoaging as a consensus-endorsed indication.
caveat: The endorsed indications emphasized neuropathy, alopecia, ulcers, pain, and radiation dermatitis rather than routine cosmetic photoaging protocols.

headline: This consensus says PBM is generally safe when used as directed, emphasizes red and NIR wavelength ranges, and treats parameter reporting as essential rather than optional.
implication: Useful for conservative safety language, parameter-field completeness, and avoiding overclaiming from broad PBM literature.
caveat: Broad PBM guideline rather than direct whole-body red/NIR efficacy testing, and the literature search stopped in June 2022.

headline: Umbrella review found the strongest fibromyalgia support for fatigue, while several other fibromyalgia endpoints remained low or very low certainty or nonsignificant.
implication: Useful for certainty grading and null-result boundaries, not for direct whole-body protocol claims.
caveat: Mixed conditions and modalities; most outcomes were low or very low certainty; no high-certainty outcome was identified.

headline: A single 12-minute whole-body red and near-infrared PBM session increased resting energy expenditure in women with obesity, but not as a generic across-population efficacy signal.
implication: Useful for dose, timing, and metabolic-endpoint design in obesity-like cohorts while keeping claims acute and population-specific.
caveat: Women-only small crossover study; normal-weight participants did not show the same clear metabolic gain, RER was unchanged, and no long-term outcomes were measured.

headline: Systematic review of chronic-pain RCTs found many positive pain signals and generally low reported adverse-event burden, but directness to whole-body red/NIR exposure was low.
implication: Useful as broader chronic-pain context and for safety cross-checking, not as direct protocol evidence.
caveat: Mixed pain conditions, mixed delivery modes, variable device parameters, and no meta-analysis.

headline: USPSTF recommends counseling to reduce ultraviolet exposure and avoid indoor tanning, reinforcing the UV-risk boundary.
implication: This keeps indoor-tanning behavior and UV-risk evidence distinct from therapeutic red/NIR whole-body PBM.
caveat: This recommendation addresses ultraviolet exposure prevention, not therapeutic light treatment.

headline: WHO places artificial tanning devices in a UV-risk and public-health-regulation domain rather than a therapeutic PBM domain.
implication: This is a high-value safety boundary source to prevent sunbed or tanning-device analogies from entering whole-body red/NIR protocol copy.
caveat: This source concerns UV-emitting tanning devices, not therapeutic red/NIR devices.

headline: Cochrane blue-light filtering lens evidence is an adjacent light-intervention boundary, not whole-body red/NIR PBM evidence.
implication: Use this source to keep eyewear, eye-strain, macular-health, and blue-light-filtering sleep claims separate from whole-body PBM claims.
caveat: Spectacle-lens trials are not whole-body photobiomodulation and should not be promoted into direct efficacy evidence for this protocol.
